# pi-fixed-supply

> Pi's total native supply is exactly 100,000,000,000 π on every observable ledger, and no operation
> in the network's current protocol increases it.

Repository: https://github.com/aybvip/pi-fixed-supply
Site:       https://aybvip.github.io/pi-fixed-supply/
Licence:    MIT (code and text). Quoted Pi Network / Stellar documentation belongs to its authors.
Status:     self-tested; NOT independently audited.

## What is claimed

- Claim A (proven): Pi Mainnet's TOTAL native supply is fixed at 100,000,000,000 π on every observable
  ledger — from ledger 2 (2020-12-31T22:47:31Z) to the live head. Measured: 70 ledgers sampled across
  the full range, 0 deviations from `total_coins = 100000000000.0000000`.
- Claim B (verifiable): any single ledger's supply can be read from its raw consensus-signed
  `header_xdr`, independently of the API's JSON summary. The decoder also reads `inflationSeq`, which
  the JSON does not expose; it is 0.
- Claim C (NOT claimed): circulating / "effective" supply, allocation, unlock schedules, price,
  consensus. Pi defines Effective Total Supply separately as Migrated Mining Rewards / 65%.

## What is NOT claimed

- That circulating supply equals 100,000,000,000 π (it does not; that is a different, off-ledger figure).
- That `total_coins` equals the sum of all account balances (it is a header field; no sum is claimed).
- That the supply can never change under any future protocol. Pi's Whitepaper explicitly reserves the
  question of future inflation for a later community decision. The claim is scoped to the CURRENT
  protocol and the OBSERVABLE PRESENT.
- Anything about ledgers before ledger 2: ledger 1 returns HTTP 410 Gone and is not served.
- Anything about price, value, legality, or investment merit. Not financial advice.

## Key facts

- Documented maximum supply: 100,000,000,000 π (Pi Network blog, 2025-04-17; Pi Whitepaper, 2021-12-28).
- 1 π = 10,000,000 stroops — derived from the chain: raw `totalCoins` = 1000000000000000000 stroops.
- Ledger 2 (first observable): `total_coins` already at the cap; `fee_pool` = 0; `inflationSeq` = 0.
- Ledger 1: HTTP 410 Gone (the lower bound of the claim).
- `fee_pool` grows from 0.0000000 at genesis to about 11,780,946.9229664 at the head, while
  `total_coins` never moves — a fee sink, not issuance.
- Protocol versions seen across the sampled range: 0, 15, 18, 19, 21, 24, 25, 26, 28.
- Several other header fields DID change over the same range (baseFee 100 -> 100000, baseReserve
  100000000 -> 4900000, maxTxSetSize 100 -> 1000) while `totalCoins` and `inflationSeq` did not — so the
  measurement is not blind.
- Stellar removed the `inflation` operation — the protocol's only native-issuance operation — at
  Protocol 12, on 2019-10-28, before Pi's genesis.

## How to verify (read-only, GET only, zero dependencies, Node 18+)

    node examples/run-all.mjs                 # everything, one verdict
    node examples/xdr-header.mjs              # decode the raw header, cross-check the API
    node examples/xdr-header.mjs 2            # the earliest observable ledger
    node examples/supply-check.mjs --samples 40
    node examples/op-check.mjs
    node examples/self-test.mjs               # the test suite (~62 checks)
    node examples/self-test.mjs --offline     # no network at all

Without Node at all:

    curl -s https://api.mainnet.minepi.com/ledgers/2 | grep -o '"total_coins":"[^"]*"'
    curl -s https://api.mainnet.minepi.com/ledgers?order=desc&limit=1 | grep -o '"total_coins":"[^"]*"'

Both print "total_coins":"100000000000.0000000".

## Falsifiers — how to prove this wrong

- F1: a ledger whose `total_coins` is not exactly 100000000000.0000000.
- F2: an operation that creates native π, or a transaction that raises `total_coins`.
- F3: a ledger where the API's `total_coins` differs from the decoded raw `header_xdr`.
- F4: a protocol change that re-enables native issuance (anticipated, not denied).
- F5: a pre-genesis (ledger 1) signed header that disagrees.

Only F1-F3 end the claim today. Objections about price, circulating supply, allocation or consensus are
NOT falsifiers — they are answers to different questions.
